newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Westin aims to open 16 new hotels in Asia by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Westin aims to open 16 new hotels in Asia by 2000.

text.p: Seattle-based Westin Hotels and Resorts said on Monday 50 percent of its growth would be outside of the United States and the group aims to operate 35 hotels in the Asia Pacific by year 2000, company officials said.
"We would have 35 hotels by 2000," Ted Teng, president of the Asia Pacific unit of Westin told a news conference here.
The company plans to open 16 new hotels in addition to the 19 it currently operates in Asia, he added.
Teng said their aggressive expansion programme saw two new hotels open this year in Surabaya, Indonesia and Bangkok, Thailand. He added another hotel in Guam would be ready by the end of the year.
Two more hotels are in the pipeline for 1998 in Jakarta, Indonesia and Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The other hotels will go up in Australia, India, Hong Kong, China and Taiwan.
No details of investment costs were given.
Asia, which represents 20 percent of the group's total room capacity, contributes 22 percent of the group's total revenue.
